## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

We need a self-contained web app. Options: Three.js via CDN or install three from npm. Network access? Let's test npm. We need complete playable game with procedural 3D room, procedural 3D Pokémon, procedural moves in 3 groups. Build with Three.js. If npm available, use vite + three. But simpler: static index.html with importmap to CDN? Offline capture may have network restrictions. Better install three via npm and use Vite build to static dist. Let's check npm registry access.

Also need playwright screenshot capability for my checks: playwright-cli open etc. We can use capture.sh infrastructure maybe easier: start server via `npm run dev` or vite preview on port 3002 and playwright-cli. Agents.md says use port 3002 and playwright-cli. Let's set up.

Plan game design:

Title: "CHAMPIONS: Rift Arena" — Pokémon Champions-inspired 3D creature battler.

Core:
- Procedurally generated 3D battle room: arena with floor, walls, pillars, crystals, lighting, fog, particle motes, audience? Generated seed.
- Procedural 3D Pokémon: creature generated from seed: body shape, head, eyes, limbs, tail, horns, colors, patterns, element type, name. Need visually appealing low-poly monsters.
- Procedural moves in 3 groups: Physical, Special, Status. Each move generated with name, group/category, element, power, accuracy, PP, description, VFX. 3 groups explicit tabs maybe.
- Gameplay: turn-based battle vs AI champion. Player has a team of 3 procedurally generated creatures; enemy has 3. Select moves, use items? "Pokémon champions clone" — team of 3, choose move, type effectiveness, stats, status effects, switching. Need complete playable loop: start screen, room, encounter, battle, win/lose, rematch with new seed.

Make it polished: 3D scene with camera transitions between "room overview" and battle stance. UI overlays: HUD, move cards grouped in 3 columns (PHYSICAL / SPECIAL / STATUS), HP bars, turn log, effects, damage numbers. Procedural generation shown in start screen with "Generate New Rift" and seed.

Simplify but deep enough:
- Stats: HP, ATK, DEF, SP.ATK, SP.DEF, SPD.
- Elements with effectiveness chart maybe 6 types (Ember, Tide, Verdant, Volt, Umbra, Lumen). Procedural creature types.
- Moves: 3 per creature (one each group) + maybe 4. Requirement "procedurally generated Pokémon moves that follow in 3 groups" — ensure UI has three groups. Each creature gets 3 moves: one physical, one special, one status. Maybe 6 moves, 2 per group. Better 3 per group? That's 9 move cards too many. Use 6 moves: 2 per group. But battle UI with 3 group tabs, each has 2 moves. That strongly demonstrates groups.

Status moves: buff ATK, shield, heal, speed, debuff enemy, burn/poison. Physical/special moves damage.

Battle flow: player's active creature, enemy active. Player picks move → resolves player then enemy AI picks → animate. Switching allowed (bench panel). Team of 3 each. Win when all enemy fainted. Champion "Rift Warden" with 3 mons. Player first picks starter from 3 generated creatures? Champions uses team building. We can start with "Choose your Rift Trio" — generate 3 creatures, player picks 1 of 3 squads? Maybe simpler: start screen shows 3 generated starter creatures, choose one; then other two join automatically as squad. Or show team of 3 and let user choose lead. That's nice: "Choose your lead" with 3 cards rendered in 3D preview? Could do 2D cards with canvas portraits generated from creature seed. Could render portraits using small WebGL canvases — expensive. Instead use CSS/SVG creature sigils derived from seed. But the 3D models are the core; we can show them in the room on pedestals before battle, and clicking a creature selects lead. Nice.

Scene design: One continuous Three.js scene:
- "Sanctum" room: hexagonal arena, floor with rings, pillars, floating crystals, fog, stars. Camera at an angle.
- Player creatures stand on left platform, enemy on right, active creature center-left/right facing each other. Initially room shows 3 pedestals with player's team? Hmm.
- Intro: hero screen overlay "RIFT CHAMPIONS" with seed and button "Enter the Rift". Clicking generates room and creatures.
- Team select: 3 generated creature models on pedestals in room, click one to lead. Enemy team preview silhouettes.
- Battle: camera moves to arena view. Active creatures at battle positions, others hidden or on bench. Move selection grouped tabs. Animations: lunge, projectile VFX, flashes, shake, damage numbers, status particles. Enemy AI with simple scoring.
- Victory screen with stats, "New Rift" (regenerate everything), "Rematch".

Sound: WebAudio procedural synth for clicks, hits, cries, victory. Nice.

Procedural creature generation: Need solid 3D shapes. Approach: build from primitives with rounded look, using low-poly geometry and flatShading. Body forms: quadruped, biped, serpent, floating orb, insectoid. Add:
- body ellipsoid, head sphere, snout, eyes (white + pupil), ears/horns, arms, legs, tail (segmented cones/spheres), wings, spikes, fins, crystal shards, patterns (spots/stripes via small flattened spheres on body?), aura particles, glow. Material colors from palette with secondary/accent. Type influences parts (e.g., Verdant leaves, Tide fins, Ember horns/flame, Volt spikes, Umbra wisps, Lumen halo).
- Size scaled per species; proportions random.
- Idle animation: bob, breathe, tail sway, ear twitch, eyes blink.
- Use groups for animation parts (head, tail, arms, wings, body). Store references.

Procedural room generation:
- Arena radius, floor style (hex/tiles), wall ring with pillars count, arches, floating crystals, banners with procedural sigil, torches/light orbs, audience silhouettes? fog color. Generate based on seed. Keep visual quality high.
- Use MeshStandardMaterial, tone mapping ACES, shadows, contact-ish blob shadows, point lights. Performance must be OK in SwiftShader (software rendering!). Need moderate poly count and no postprocessing. Avoid too many shadow lights. One directional light with shadows + point lights without shadows.

UI: HTML/CSS overlay. Fonts: use system + Google font? Offline concerns; use CSS font stacks with "Cinzel" fallback? Can't rely. Could embed via Google Fonts network maybe blocked. Use built-in serif/display: Georgia, "Trebuchet MS". Design with gradients, glass panels, glow. High polish.

Need build setup. Let's check npm network and whether vite/three available globally.

UI:

- Enemy panel top-left? Standard: enemy info top-left/right, player bottom-right. Since 3D scene, HUD panels anchored top-left (enemy) and bottom-right (player) plus move tray bottom center/left.

- Selected a dark, gold-accented fantasy arena presentation with complete title, team-selection, battle, codex, and end screens.
